audit: The railway control-room analogy explains coordination but leaves the difference between instructions, selected evidence and retained execution authority abstract. Lesson A gives a single run three concrete workspaces, including a released definition, a stale balance observation and an unresolved intent. It asks which owner must repair the discrepancy. Lesson B follows an approved refund across cancellation while the payment service is already processing it. The final record distinguishes stopped future scheduling from a confirmed completed effect. This directly addresses the chapter's cancellation and outcome-verification corrections without implying that a harness can physically interrupt every external transaction.

lessons.title: Three records for one controlled journey
lessons.intro: ShopAssist run R-42 has a stale balance observation and a saved refund intent awaiting reconciliation. Inspect what each owner actually retains.

relations: View supplies facts; brief guides proposals.
The control record governs the next action.

read: The brief says how to behave, not what the current balance is.
The observation has a timestamp and may need refreshing.
The unresolved intent must be reconciled before another refund.
lessons.question: Would adding stronger refund wording to the brief resolve intent K-17?
lessons.answer: No. The executor must use the retained effect identity and the payment service's status or deduplication contract to resolve K-17. The context builder can then supply updated evidence. Instructions cannot reconstruct a lost external outcome.
lessons.takeaway: Fix the owner of the failed contract: guidance, evidence or execution state.
lessons.assumption: Fictional run; the control-room analogy describes coordination, not physical control of an external service.

lessons.title: Cancellation arrives after submission
lessons.intro: The exact refund passed approval, authority and budget checks. Cancellation arrives after submission but before the service reports its result.

data.result: Run cancelled; RF-9 confirmed; no later tools scheduled.

read: Intent persistence precedes the external submission.
Cancellation prevents future scheduling once observed.
The committed refund remains a fact after cancellation.
lessons.question: If the final receipt cannot be retrieved, may the cancellation message say no refund occurred?
lessons.answer: No. Submission already occurred, so the outcome remains unknown until reconciliation establishes it. Retain K-17 and the cancellation reason, stop new work, and communicate the uncertainty. Cancellation is not proof of rollback or non-execution.
lessons.takeaway: Stopping future work and discovering an in-flight outcome are separate responsibilities.
lessons.assumption: Fictional ordered events; service processing is non-cancellable here. Equal spacing shows sequence, not proportional elapsed duration.
